headline: Launch A: it leads by 1.4 points and is 70% likely to be the better version. A sharper Version C could widen the gap.

variants.label: Version A
variants.text: New: Oat Milk Honey Latte, $6.50. Made with local wildflower honey. On the menu now at South Congress Coffee.

targeting.note: Core segment South Congress specialty coffee drinkers 18-44 first; the crowd sampled 50.0% core.

plan.success_metric: Taps through to the post and store visits attributed to the post (the real-world counterpart of the simulated intent to visit).
plan.decision_rule: Keep version A running if its tap rate is not below the simulated range; otherwise pause it.
plan.stop_rule: Stop after 2,700 people have seen it, or after 7 days.
assumptions: These are simulated people, not real customers; the backtest shows the crowd does not reliably predict real winners.
Audience size is an estimate: ACS adults in the ZIP times national Pew Instagram use by age.

reasons: A leads on intent to visit: 24.8% vs 23.4%, a 1.4-point gap with a 95% interval of ±5.1 points, and A is ahead in 2 of 2 seeds. A is 70% likely to be the better version.
A live split test would need about 14,637 people per version (108.4% of the local Instagram users) and paid impressions to detect this gap. Ripple ran it on the simulated crowd for $0 of ad spend.
There are about 27,006 Instagram users in Austin, TX 78704 (Census x Pew join).
A sharper Version C, drafted from what people objected to, could widen the gap. It is worth acting on only if it moves intent by at least 3.4 points, the smallest gap that would be worth acting on.
C moved intent +1.0 pts vs A on the same crowd (30.1% vs 29.0%): keep A. The bar is 3.6 pts, the smallest gap that would be worth acting on.
note: Exported by Dry Run. Nothing was posted or spent.
